blocks.text: 1. Cross-Attention
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445883213-945415636.png

Self-Attention, the previous topic, covered attending within a single sequence. Cross-Attention gives a closer contrast between attending within one sequence versus between two, explored throughout this topic.
It formally names the exact mechanism already covered generally in Encoder-Decoder Attention, giving that earlier, informally described technique its own precise, standard terminology.
2. Recapping The Two Setups

This connects back to Self-Attention and Encoder-Decoder Attention, both already covered. Self-Attention operates within one sequence; Encoder-Decoder Attention operates between two sequences, already covered in those two earlier topics.
This topic genuinely gives that second case its own precise, standard name: Cross-Attention, formalizing the distinction already implicitly covered throughout this module.
3. The Formal Definition
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445883213-999203081.png

The genuinely precise definition connects back to Query, Key, and Value, already covered in their own topic. Query genuinely comes from one sequence; Key and Value genuinely come from a genuinely different sequence.
This genuinely precise structural description, already covered in this section, is exactly what distinguishes Cross-Attention from the single-sequence setup already covered in Self-Attention.

5. Self-Attention Versus Cross-Attention, Directly Compared
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445883214-639257246.png

This connects back to Self-Attention's own single-sequence setup, already covered in its own topic. Self-Attention genuinely draws Query, Key, and Value all from the exact same sequence, already covered there.
Cross-Attention genuinely draws them from two genuinely different sequences instead, the exact structural distinction already covered throughout the rest of this topic.
6. The Direction Of Information Flow
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445883822-572695746.png

A genuinely important interpretive detail connects back to context-aware representations, already covered in Self-Attention. Cross-Attention genuinely lets one sequence's own representations be genuinely shaped by information from an entirely different sequence.
This is a genuinely important interpretive extension of the context-awareness already covered there, now spanning across two genuinely distinct sequences rather than staying confined within just one.

10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates computing Cross-Attention between two genuinely different sequences, contrasting it directly with the Self-Attention computation already covered in the previous topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
hidden_size = 4

sequence_a = rng.normal(size=(3, hidden_size))  # genuinely sequence one, already covered as producing the Query
sequence_b = rng.normal(size=(5, hidden_size))  # genuinely a different sequence, already covered as producing Key and Value

W_query = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1
W_key = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1
W_value = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1

# already covered as the formal definition in this topic
queries = sequence_a @ W_query.T          # from sequence_a
keys = sequence_b @ W_key.T                # from sequence_b, a genuinely different sequence
values = sequence_b @ W_value.T            # also from sequence_b

def softmax(x):
    exp_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    return exp_x / exp_x.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)

scores = queries @ keys.T / np.sqrt(hidden_size)
attention_weights = softmax(scores)
output = attention_weights @ values

print(f"Sequence A length: {sequence_a.shape[0]}, Sequence B length: {sequence_b.shape[0]}, already covered as two genuinely different sequences")
print(f"Attention weights shape: {attention_weights.shape}")
print(f"Output shape (matches sequence A's own length, already covered as the formal definition in this topic): {output.shape}")

blocks.content: Running this example shows the output shape matching sequence A's own length, since the Query came from there, while the attention weights span sequence B's own length, exactly the formal definition already covered in this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Cross-Attention formally names attention between two genuinely different sequences.
Query comes from one sequence; Key and Value come from a genuinely different sequence.
Encoder-Decoder Attention was Cross-Attention all along, just without this precise name yet.
Self-Attention draws Query, Key, and Value from the same sequence; Cross-Attention draws them from two.
It lets one sequence's representations be shaped by information from an entirely different sequence.
Many real architectures combine both Self-Attention and Cross-Attention together.
It becomes especially valuable connecting different data types, like images and text.
It is a core mechanism for Machine Translation and Multimodal Deep Learning alike.
Next up: Multi-Head Attention, running several attention computations in parallel for richer representations.
